meaning: The number 41 has no prominent symbolic meaning in biblical tradition.
description: Unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40 and 42, which carry rich symbolism in the Bible, the number 41 has no known independent symbolic role. It appears in concrete biblical contexts: Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king of Judah (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chronicles 12:13), and King Asa died in his 41st year of reign (2 Chronicles 16:13). These occurrences are, however, chronological in nature and are not attributed any special spiritual or mystical meaning in tradition. The number's placement between the symbolically charged numbers 40 and 42 makes it strikingly neutral – it marks neither the completion of a period of testing (40) nor a new beginning.

versions.meaning: The number 41 has no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: Unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40, and 42, which carry rich symbolism in the Bible, the number 41 has no known independent symbolic role. It appears occasionally in genealogies and chronologies (for example, some kings reigned for periods close to 41 years), but this is not attributed any special spiritual or mystical significance. In Jewish numerology (gematria), any number can be linked to Hebrew words, but 41 has no widely recognized symbolic tradition associated with it.
versions.reason: [minor] The description mentions that "some kings reigned for periods close to 41 years," but there is actually a more precise example: Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king (1 Kings 14:21, 2 Chronicles 12:13), and Asa died in his 41st year of reign (2 Chronicles 16:13). This could have been mentioned more specifically to strengthen the text.; [minor] It would have been useful to include a footnote about the gematria value of the number 41 and the Hebrew word אם (em, 'mother'), which has a gematria value of 41 (alef=1, mem=40). This is a relevant linguistic point that belongs in a footnote.; [minor] The phrasing "no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning" in meaning is a bit long. It could be tightened somewhat, but it is not incorrect.

footnotes.text: In Hebrew gematria, the word אם (em, 'mother') has the value 41 (alef = 1, mem = 40). Rehoboam's age at his accession as a 41-year-old is mentioned in both places together with his mother Naama, but there is no established tradition linking this gematria value to the biblical context.
The number 41 is a prime number, which in certain Kabbalistic traditions may give it a character of indivisible wholeness, but even this has not granted 41 any broad symbolic recognition.
